title: Input Capture & Drag and Drop
summary: Share the mouse and keyboard between ImGui and your engine, query item state, build custom hit areas and drag meshes, colours and entities around the editor.

quiz.q: The user is typing an entity name in an InputText and presses W. How should the engine know not to move the camera?
options: It can't; disable WASD while the editor is open
quiz.explain: io.WantCaptureKeyboard is true while ImGui owns the keyboard: an active text field, a modal, or (with keyboard navigation on, as in OGL.c) any focused ImGui window. Skip engine keyboard handling while it is set.

quiz.q: When does AcceptDragDropPayload("MESH_TYPE") return a non-NULL payload (with default flags)?
options: Every frame the source is dragged
When a payload of that type is released over the target
When any payload hovers the target
Only when the source calls EndDragDropSource()
quiz.explain: By default it returns the payload only on delivery, the frame the mouse is released over the target. Use ImGuiDragDropFlags_AcceptBeforeDelivery to peek earlier.

quiz.q: Why does the reorder code store moveFrom/moveTo and apply them after the loop?
options: Drag and drop only works outside loops
Changing the array while iterating and drawing it would mix up rows and IDs for that frame
quiz.explain: Deferring structural changes until after iteration is a standard pattern. The capstone lesson uses it for deletes too.

quiz.q: What payload type does ColorEdit4 send when you drag its colour square?
quiz.explain: Colour widgets use the built-in "_COL3F"/"_COL4F" types, so your own targets can accept colours from any colour widget.
